text:
tom: opened PR #5334 to clarify Orion-XL quant cold-start behavior and add an SDK v4 example + small bench table. preview: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5334

ivy: quick summary: some customers reported huge first-token latency after a model switch to the quant variant. need a short explanation + recommended mitigation (warmup vs persistent instance).

priya: can you paste the bench numbers? i'll format a tiny table. also note the SDK param rename: v3 `warmup_tokens` -> v4 `prefill_tokens`. docs should use v4.

tom: numbers from a quick p3dn run (batch=1):
- cold first token (quant): 1.8s
- warm first token (quant, after warmup): 180ms
- cold first token (non-quant): 600ms
CSV: https://drive.google.com/orion-xl-quant-coldstart.csv

sam: nit: explain briefly why this happens (kernel JIT + memory page faults on quant kernels) and show two mitigations: 1) run a short warmup generate of ~32 tokens at startup, 2) use dedicated/pinned instance for critical low-latency paths.

priya: SDK v4 snippet suggestion (js):
```js
// quick warmup to avoid cold first-token spike
await client.generate({ model: "orion-xl-quant", input: "Warmup.", prefill_tokens: 32 });
```

ivy: also add a one-line compatibility note: some adapter-quant variants don't support kernel caching across restarts; mention test steps to verify.

tom: good call. i'll add a short "How to reproduce" section for SEs + a migration note for Dedicated customers to pin non-quant during evals. pushing update now.

docbot: docs-lint: passed \u2705 preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/5334/ (staging)

priya: left a small wording nit: prefer "first-token latency" rather than "cold first token" for clarity.

sam: +1

ivy: +1

tom: thanks all, merging after CI. follow-up: add automated cold-start check to the perf suite. :rocket:
